questions.title: Sports-day spreadsheet analysis
questions.intro: Houses record the number of participants: B2=18, B3=24, B4=28, B5=30. Column C will show a category.

parts.prompt: Name suitable functions for total participants, average entries per house and smallest value.
House values B2:B5 are 18, 24, 28 and 30. Write a SUM formula in B6.
Calculate the total participants.
Write an AVERAGE formula for B2:B5.
Calculate the mean number per house.
Write a COUNTIF formula counting houses with 25 or more participants.
Give the COUNTIF result.
Write an IF formula in C2 that outputs "Large" if B2 is at least 25, otherwise "Small".
State the output for the first house.
The organiser will give more resources only to Large houses. Evaluate the decision using one number, one limitation, one extra type of evidence and a recommendation.
Explain the purpose of a diamond, a rectangle and a parallelogram in a flowchart.
In a flowchart, a decision is 'hours >= 2?'. Yes outputs 'Extended'; No outputs 'Standard'. Explain the outputs for hours=2 and hours=1.
Trace: Input speed=55; if speed>60 then output 'Slow down', otherwise output 'Within limit'. State path and output.
Design a flowchart to input stock quantity, select "Reorder" when stock is 10 or below and "Enough" otherwise, then output the chosen label.
This code should label positive values but instead tests `if value < 0: print('Positive')`. Identify the logic error and correct it.
Write a Python program using constants PASS = 50 and MERIT = 80. Input a whole-number score; print "Merit" for 80+, "Pass" for 50–79, and "Retry" below 50.
Name two boundary tests that together verify both thresholds, with expected outputs.
Identify a suitable input for an image model that detects plant leaf damage.
Describe how labelled healthy and damaged-leaf photos help model training.
Give two practical AR overlays for staff checking irrigation equipment.

Training photographs were all taken in bright sunshine, but the model performs poorly in shade. Evaluate replacing staff checks, giving a benefit, limitation, mitigation and recommendation.
